description: Given you probably wouldn't want to rock up to a modern battlefield with a spear and chainmail, it's hopefully not controversial to say that tech can be critical to a nation's military edge. But at procurement level, it can get complicated. New techs often battle teething issues and may never live up to expectations leaving countries burning resources on a change that never delivers. In other cases, good ideas are ignored or under-funded because of tradition, incumbency or flawed assessments. And so today, we're going to talk about the nature of picking winners in the tech race and some of the many, many ways that nations have historically sometimes got it wrong.
